Calculadora de condensadores planos, cil: Calculator for parallel-plate, cylindrical and spherical capacitors with dielectrics: capacitance with layers in series or in parallel, charge, voltage, energy, E, D and P fields, polarization charges and what happens when the dielectric is inserted, step by step.
¿Cómo se calcula la capacidad de un cond: How is the capacitance of a capacitor calculated?
Plano: C = ε₀εᵣA/d. Cilíndrico: C = 2πε₀: Parallel plate: C = ε₀εᵣA/d. Cylindrical: C = 2πε₀εᵣL/ln(b/a). Spherical: C = 4πε₀εᵣ·ab/(b − a). For example, an air parallel-plate capacitor with A = 100 cm² and d = 1 mm has C = 8.85·10⁻¹² · 0.01 / 0.001 ≈ 88.5 pF.
¿Cómo se calcula su energía y qué pasa a: How is its energy calculated and what happens when a dielectric is inserted?
U = ½CV² = Q²/(2C). Un dieléctrico multi: U = ½CV² = Q²/(2C). A dielectric multiplies the capacitance by εᵣ: if the battery stays connected, V is constant and Q increases; if it was disconnected, Q is constant and V is divided by εᵣ. With C = 88.5 pF at 100 V, U = ½ · 88.5·10⁻¹² · 100² ≈ 4.4·10⁻⁷ J.

Un dieléctrico es un aislante cuyas molé: A dielectric is an insulator whose molecules become polarized in the field: polarization charges appear on its faces, of opposite sign to the plate next to them, which weaken the field inside. So, with the same free charge, the field and the voltage drop by a factor ε<sub>r</sub>, and the capacitance rises by that same factor.

Capas en serie y en paralelo: Layers in series and in parallel
Si las capas se suceden en el sentido de: If the layers follow one another in the direction of the field (one slab next to another between the plates), D is the same in all of them and each layer is a capacitor in series: 1/C = Σ 1/C<sub>i</sub>. If the dielectric fills only part of the area but the whole thickness, all the parts have the same voltage and are capacitors in parallel: C = Σ C<sub>i</sub>.
<b>Con la batería</b>, V se mantiene: al: With the battery, V is kept constant: when the dielectric is inserted the charge and the energy increase. The battery does work ΔQ·V, twice the increase in energy; the other half is the work done by the field pulling the dielectric in.
<b>Aislado</b>, Q se mantiene: la tensió: Isolated, Q is kept constant: the voltage and the energy decrease. The missing energy is the work of the field on the dielectric.
Si el dieléctrico ocupa una parte del án: If the dielectric fills part of the angle (for example, half a sphere with $ε_{r1}$ and the other half with $ε_{r2}$), each part goes from one plate to the other and all are at the same voltage: they are capacitors in parallel. E does not depend on the dielectric, only D and the free charge: $C = 4π ε_0 {a b}/{b − a} · (f_1 ε_{r1} + f_2 ε_{r2})$, with $f_i$ the fraction of the surface.
Con $ε_r(x)$ variable, D sigue saliendo: With variable $ε_r(x)$, D still comes from Gauss and $1/C = ∫ dx/(ε_0 ε_r(x) S)$. In the parallel plate with $ε_r$ linear between $ε_1$ and $ε_2$: $C = {ε_0 S (ε_2 − ε_1)}/{d ln(ε_2/ε_1)}$. Since P is not uniform, besides the polarization charges on the faces there is volume charge, $ρ_p = −∇·P$.
Las armaduras se atraen con $F = Q^2/(2: The plates attract each other with $F = Q^2/(2 ε_0 S)$. A dielectric half inserted is pushed in with $F = 1/2 V^2 {dC}/{dx}$. Each material withstands a maximum field, its dielectric strength (about 3 kV/mm for air): the maximum voltage is the one that takes the region with the most field relative to its strength to that limit.
Fuerza sobre la lámina que entra: Force on the slab being inserted
Con una lámina de $ε_r$ metida una longi: With a slab of $ε_r$ inserted a length x between plates of length a and width w, $C(x) = {ε_0 w (ε_r x + a − x)}/d$. With the battery (V fixed) the force pulling it in is $F = 1/2 V^2 {dC}/{dx}$, constant; with fixed charge, $F = −{dU}/{dx} = {Q^2}/{2C^2} {dC}/{dx}$, which decreases as it enters. The battery's work, $V ΔQ$, is twice the increase in energy $ΔU$; the other half is the mechanical work. If it is the distance between plates that changes with the slab filling the gap, $F = U/d$.
En una asociación las tensiones de todos: In a combination the voltages of all the capacitors are proportional to the applied voltage. If each withstands $V_{break,i}$ and carries $V_i$, the network withstands $V · V_{break,i}/V_i$ according to that capacitor, and the maximum voltage of the network is the smallest. In series, the one that carries the most voltage relative to what it withstands breaks first, which is usually the one with the lowest capacitance.
En serie todos tienen la misma carga y $: In series all have the same charge and $1/C_eq = Σ 1/C_i$; in parallel, the same voltage and $C_eq = Σ C_i$. When two charged capacitors are connected the charge is conserved and shared until the voltages are equal, but energy is lost in the connection.
